html:
SMTO-POL-0034 — An older permission question was closed by your new message

GUID: 31f6397a-3e17-5788-828f-f681e07cd1fc
Slug: authority-request-superseded
Domain: POL · Subsystem: resource-access

What happened

  • You updated your request while SMTO was waiting for a permission answer. The old question no longer fits, so SMTO closed it. Nothing new was allowed, and access you gave earlier is unchanged.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Read SMTO's next reply to your updated request. SMTO is now working on what you asked most recently, not on the older plan.
  2. If a new permission card appears, read it and choose Authorize this resource for this task or Don't allow. Any access the updated request needs gets its own question, separate from the closed one.
  3. Don't go looking for the old question to answer it. It was closed, and an answer to it would not apply to your updated request.

What success looks like

  • The task continues without waiting on the old question, and any new access shows its own card.

If it still fails

  • If the task stays stuck waiting, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't assume the closed question was approved, or that permissions you gave earlier were removed.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Applied user steering changed the task intent, so the unanswered resource-access request for the previous intent was marked superseded and its wait was closed.

What this means

  • The resource request's saved source digest no longer matches current task intent. The controller marks that request and its authority question superseded and closes a matching waiting activity. Previously issued grants are retained; retirement does not authorize the new intent.

Why this can happen

  • The resource request's saved source digest no longer matches current task intent. The controller marks that request and its authority question superseded and closes a matching waiting activity. Previously issued grants are retained; retirement does not authorize the new intent.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the superseded request with the applied user input and the currently pending authority question.

How to fix it

  • No action is needed on the superseded request: retire_superseded completes its authority request as superseded and closes any waiting activity. Review any new request_resource_access question raised for the updated intent; earlier grants are retained but do not authorize the new intent.
  • Follow the updated task and review any new permission question it presents.

Retry and execution caution

  • Do not retry the superseded question; the updated task owns any new request.

How to verify the fix

  • The obsolete question no longer blocks the task, and any new access has its own current question.

What not to do

  • Do not answer the obsolete question or infer that existing grants were revoked or new access approved.

Technical notes

  • The old wait is closed without granting access or revoking previously issued grants.
  • Supersession does not establish the outcome of earlier task operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
